summary.tldr: Creates a federal medal for people who donate an organ during their lifetime without profiting from it.
what_it_does: Establishes the Living Donor Recognition Medal for eligible people who donate an organ, including tissue, blood, or bone marrow, during their lifetime without profiting.
Lets the Governor in Council set the medal’s design and ribbon.
Allows the Governor General to award the medal, and says no person can receive it more than once.
Calls for the medal to be given, when possible, in a public ceremony by specified officials or other prescribed representatives.
Lets the Governor in Council make rules on who is eligible and which entities can assess eligibility or help with it.
summary.background: The bill defines “organ” to include human tissue, blood and bone marrow. It also lets the Governor in Council make regulations about eligibility and related assessment.
